stories.title: Nepal flash flood washes away villages, project sites near Tibet border
stories.summary: A massive flash flood in the Himalayan nation of Nepal washed away villages and project sites in a region bordering Tibet, authorities said on Wednesday, warning of heavy casualties as they urged those living on river banks to seek higher ground. The areas of Syapru Besi and Timure in the mountainous district of Rasuwa were severely affected, government officials said, while calling for extra vigilance by residents along the Bhote Koshi river. "We have reports of villages and infrastructure project sites being washed away," district administrator. Narendra Pariyar told Reuters, adding that no immediate estimates of casualties or property losses were available. "There could be heavy casualties or loss of property," he said. "But I cannot say for sure now." Prime Minister Balendra Shah said rescue and relief teams, as well as police and the military had been dispatched to help in the aid effort. "Instructions have been given... to move the people living in the lower areas to safer places," he said. "People along the river are advised to exercise extra caution and remain alert," the government said in its statement. The Bhote Koshi river originates in Tibet and empties into Nepal's Trishuli river that eventually flows into India as the Gandak river. A flood last year in the Bhote Koshi river killed nine people, with 24 missing, and washed away the 'Friendship Bridge' linking Nepal and China to disrupt transport and trade for several months.

stories.summary: A Hong Kong man has lost over HK$2.8 million (US$357,000) in an online investment scam in which fraudsters claiming to be employees of electricity companies duped him into investing in a “recyclable waste project”. Police also said on Wednesday that the force had recorded 50 investment scams in the past week, with losses totalling over HK$30 million. stories.title: Gov't research facilities can be used by private firm to produce ASF vaccines
stories.summary: SEOUL, Aug. 26 (Yonhap) -- Research facilities at the Animal and Plant Quarantin...
article_sentences: Research facilities at the Animal and Plant Quarantine Agency can be used by a private firm to produce African swine fever (ASF) vaccines, the state audit agency said Wednesday.

The Board of Audit and Inspection (BAI) made the assessment after a local veterinary vaccine company asked to use facilities at the animal and plant quarantine agency to produce ASF vaccines that the company had developed on its own ahead of major pharmaceutical firms.

The quarantine agency had difficulty making a decision on the request because related regulations could be interpreted to mean that the facilities may be used only for research and experimental purposes.

The agency then asked the BAI for advice, and the audit agency determined that the vaccine firm can be allowed to use the facilities as related regulations call for cooperation between the government and private entities to help commercialize technologies, among other purposes.

The BAI also noted the decision is in line with various support measures that the government is taking to help local vaccine companies gain a competitive edge in the highly competitive global vaccine market, such as expedited permits for vaccines intended for export.
